transcript: A voiceover script is text that nobody reads. They only hear it, once, at the speed it's spoken. That changes the rules.
Short sentences add weight. Longer ones carry the listener along. And give each sentence just one idea, so nobody has to hold two at once.
Full stops and questions create pauses. Use them to set up what you want remembered. So how many finished the study? Just over half.
Spoken jargon is harder to decode, because there's no time to stop. Say use, not utilise. Help, not facilitate. Define technical terms once.
Preview what's coming, mark each transition, then recap. It feels repetitive on paper. In audio, it's what keeps people with you.
Put your script in the speaker notes. On Pro, AI directs the video and times the animation to your voice. Try it at powerpoint2vid.com.
